key_findings.statement: Cataract surgery is subject to a 1-year waiting period in the first year of insurance cover.
The policy requires at least 1 year of continuous coverage with a previous insurer to waive the 1-year waiting period for specific diseases like cataract.

The insured has only 8 months of continuous coverage under the current policy and 1 year of prior coverage. The policy explicitly states it shall consider only completed years of coverage for waiver of waiting periods.
While the policy covers day care procedures, the specific waiting period exclusion for cataract surgery takes precedence over the general day care coverage provision.

citations.section: WHAT WE EXCLUDE / 3. Hospitalization expense incurred in the first year of operation of the insurance cover on treatment of the
citations.quote:
3. Hospitalization expense incurred in the first year of operation of the insurance cover on treatment of the
following Diseases:
i) Cataract
ii) Benign Prostatic Hypertrophy
iii) Myomectomy, Hysterectomy
iv) Hernia, Hydrocele
v) Fistula in anus, Piles
vi) Arthritis, Gout, Rheumatism
vii) Joint replacement unless due to accident
viii) Sinusitis and related disorders
ix) Stone in the urinary and biliary systems
x) Dilatation and Curettage
xi) Skin and all internal tumors/ cysts/ nodules/ polyps of any kind, including breast lumps unless
malignant, adenoids and hemorrhoids
xii) Dialysis required for rental failure
xiii) Surgery on tonsils and sinuses
xiv) Gastric and duodenal ulcers
However, a waiting period of 1 year will not apply if You were insured continuously and without interruption
for at least 1 year under Our or any other Indian insurer's individual health insurance Policy for the
reimbursement of medical costs for inpatient treatment in a Hospital.
NB: The reduction in the waiting period specified above shall be applied subject to the following:
 We will only apply the reduction of the waiting period if We have received the database and claim
history from the previous Indian insurance Company (if applicable);
 We are under no obligation to insure all Insured Persons or to insure all Insured Persons on the
proposed terms, or on the same terms as the previous health insurance Policy even if You have
submitted to Us all documentation
 We shall consider only completed years of coverage for waiver of waiting periods.

citations.section: WHAT WE COVER / NB4: The hospitalisation treatment of Insured Person as inpatient in the Hospital/Nursing Home for a
citations.quote:
NB4: The hospitalisation treatment of Insured Person as inpatient in the Hospital/Nursing Home for a
minimum period of 24 hours for specific treatment like Dialysis, Chemotherapy, Radiotherapy, Eye
Surgery, Lithotripsy, Tonsillectomy or D&C(medical expenses for 140 Day Care Procedures enlisted
in the Annexure to this Policy Wordings) shall also be covered under the Policy.
The minimum stay of 24 hours can be waived in other cases also provided that the following
conditions are fulfilled:
a) The treatment is such that it necessitates Hospitalisation and procedure involved requires
specialised infrastructure facilities available in the Hospital.
Or
b) Due to technological advances, the period of Hospitalisation for the treatment has been reduced to
less than 24 hours.

semantic_checks.explanation: The policy explicitly lists Cataract under the 1-year waiting period for the first year of insurance cover.
The policy requires at least 1 year of continuous, uninterrupted coverage under an Indian insurer to waive the 1-year waiting period.

The policy requires completed years of coverage for the waiver. The insured has 8 months of current coverage and 1 year of prior coverage, which does not meet the requirement for a completed year of continuous coverage under the current policy, and the waiver rule requires 1 full year of prior coverage.
The policy defines day care coverage but does not override the specific waiting period exclusions listed in the 'What We Exclude' section.
The policy limits doctor fees to 25% of the Sum Assured (500,000 * 0.25 = 125,000).
The policy limits medicines and diagnostics to 40% of the Sum Assured (500,000 * 0.40 = 200,000).
